blocking.title: ADR-0239 decision 3 overstates when /reload keeps the pick
blocking.detail: Decision 3 says /reload restores the record, and that the record and pi's live model 'differ only where the live model was never recorded - a model set on a read-only session, under the CLI's turn gate, or a placeholder'. That is false whenever the user named a model at launch (--model/--provider/--api-key/a profile model:) or the session has no conversation yet. Those rebuilds re-derive the launch inputs, which drops a recorded /model pick; pi keeps the live model. The behaviour is unchanged from base, but the new ADR text states something untrue and should name these cases.
blocking.evidence: drive.py phase T2 (tree.out/base.out): 'aelix --continue --provider anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5', '/model claude-sonnet-4-5' (recorded), '/reload', prompt. Mock: model=claude-haiku-4-5 on the tree and on the base.

blocking.title: The idle model_change's #334 queue ordering has no test row; dropping it leaves the stale model as the record
blocking.detail: core.py set_model's idle branch, 'if self._pending_session_writes or self._drain_lock.locked(): append behind the queue', is claimed in the message ('#334's queue ordering kept'). Replacing it with 'if False' (write directly) survives all 71 #376 rows and 756 harness/session tests. It is a plausible wrong implementation and it changes the restore: a cancelled release flush leaves an in-turn model_change queued, then an idle /model pick is written AHEAD of it. The session's last model_change is then the stale model, which the next --continue restores. A row like .omc/probes/376-live/r2verify/test_r2verify_probe_order.py is needed, mirroring the thinking-level C4 rows.

nonblocking.title: RPC set_model / cycle_model never record a model_change (a sibling entry point the sweep missed)
nonblocking.detail: Both handlers call harness.set_current_model, which only assigns state. pi's RPC set_model calls session.setModel and cycle_model calls cycleModel, and both append model_change. nonblocking.title: An uncatalogued id on a catalogued provider outside models.json is restored only on the user's own key; the docs describe only two cases
nonblocking.detail: restore_session_route applies route_authenticated (not a .env key) to every provider the user did not define, not only to OpenRouter. As a result, anthropic/claude-www-unlisted with only a .env key falls back, although typing the same --provider/--model at launch with that key is accepted. This is safe (stricter than the launch) and ADR-0239 decision 4 describes it, but the CHANGELOG and providers guide cover only the user-defined and OpenRouter cases.
